_meta.indication: AMITIZA is indicated for the treatment of chronic idiopathic constipation in the adult population.

pivotal_trials.design: Multi-center, parallel-group, double-blind, placebo-controlled study; following a 2-week baseline/washout period, subjects received 4 weeks of double-blind medication with no dose escalation permitted
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with chronic idiopathic constipation (predominantly female: 89.7% female in SC0131)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Frequency rate of spontaneous bowel movements (SBMs) at Week 1
pivotal_trials.result: Median Week 1 SBM frequency 5.00 for RU-0211 48 mcg vs 3.00 for placebo (Week 1 p=0.0001); the 0.3579 value is the baseline (not Week 1) p-value.

pivotal_trials.design: Multi-center, parallel-group, double-blind, placebo-controlled study; following a 2-week baseline/washout period, subjects received 4 weeks of double-blind medication with no dose escalation permitted
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with chronic idiopathic constipation (predominantly female: 88.2% female in SC0232)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Frequency rate of spontaneous bowel movements (SBMs) at Week 1
pivotal_trials.result: Median Week 1 SBM frequency 5.00 for RU-0211 48 mcg vs 3.50 for placebo (Week 1 p<0.0001); the 0.0174 value is the baseline (not Week 1) p-value.

key_safety: Across all active doses (N=1175) the most common adverse events were nausea (30.9% vs 5.1% placebo), diarrhea (13.2% vs 0.9%), headache (13.0% vs 6.6%), abdominal distension (6.8% vs 2.8%), abdominal pain (6.8% vs 2.2%), and flatulence (5.9% vs 1.9%); serious adverse events were low (2.9% RU-0211 vs 1.3% placebo).
target_moa: Lubiprostone is a locally acting chloride channel activator that specifically activates ClC-2 on the apical membrane of the human intestine, enhancing chloride-rich intestinal fluid secretion and thereby increasing intestinal motility.

description.text: Added new indication: treatment of irritable bowel syndrome with constipation (IBS-C) at 8 mcg twice daily in adult women 18 years and older

citations.quote: The medical officer recommends an approval action to be taken for oral lubiprostone 16 mcg/day (8 mcg capsules b.i.d) for the treatment of constipation predominant irritable bowel syndrome in women \ge 18 years old. Approval of Lubiprostone 16 mcg/day (8 mcg capsules bid) for the treatment of constipation predominant irritable bowel syndrome is contingent upon the sponsor incorporating the Food and Drug Administration's recommended changes to the Lubiprostone drug label and adhering to the required Phase IV commitment studies.

summary.text: Lubiprostone, a new molecular entity, received a standard review and was approved first cycle on the PDUFA goal date (January 31, 2006) for chronic idiopathic constipation in adults based on two Phase III placebo-controlled pivotal trials, with deferred pediatric studies required under PREA.

citations.quote: Lubiprostone is a prostaglandin E1 analogue and a new molecular entity.
We completed our review of this application, as amended. It is approved, effective on the date of this letter, for use as recommended in the agreed-upon labeling text.
